Deny reason appended to a 'Denied' chip in the access simulation results when the rule currently being edited caused the deny. Lowercase fragment inside a compact chip.

admin.environment.notifications.pushCont.defaultMessage:
**Generic description with only sender name** - Includes only the name of the person who sent the message in push notifications, with no information about channel name or message contents.
 **Generic description with sender and channel names** - Includes the name of the person who sent the message and the channel it was sent in, but not the message contents.
 **Full message content sent in the notification payload** - Includes the message contents in the push notification payload that is relayed through Apple's Push Notification Service (APNS) or Google's Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM). It is **highly recommended** this option only be used with an "https" protocol to encrypt the connection and protect confidential information sent in messages.

admin.environment.notifications.pushCont.defaultMessage:
**Generic description with only sender name** - Includes only the name of the person who sent the message in push notifications, with no information about channel name or message contents.
 **Generic description with sender and channel names** - Includes the name of the person who sent the message and the channel it was sent in, but not the message contents.
 **Full message content sent in the notification payload** - Includes the message contents in the push notification payload that is relayed through Apple's Push Notification Service (APNS) or Google's Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM). It is **highly recommended** this option only be used with an "https" protocol to encrypt the connection and protect confidential information sent in messages.
**Full message content fetched from the server on receipt** - The notification payload relayed through APNS or FCM contains no message content, instead it contains a unique message ID used to fetch message content from the server when a push notification is received by a device. If the server cannot be reached, a generic notification will be displayed.

admin.gitlab_feature_discovery.copy.defaultMessage: When you connect GitLab as your single sign-on provider, your team can access Mattermost without having to re-enter their GitLab credentials. Available only on Mattermost Professional and above.
admin.gitlab_feature_discovery.copy.description: Body copy on the feature discovery (upsell) page for GitLab single sign-on.

admin.gitlab_feature_discovery.title.defaultMessage: Integrate GitLab SSO with OpenID Connect in Mattermost Professional
admin.gitlab_feature_discovery.title.description: Headline on the feature discovery (upsell) page for GitLab SSO via OpenID Connect; mentions the required plan.

admin.gitlab.authTitle.description: Setting label for a text field on the GitLab OAuth admin settings; the OAuth authorization endpoint URL. Ends with a colon.

admin.gitlab.clientIdDescription.defaultMessage: Obtain this value via the instructions above for logging into GitLab.
admin.gitlab.clientIdDescription.description: Admin console help text under the GitLab Application ID field; the instructions above refers to the numbered GitLab setup steps on the same page.

admin.gitlab.clientIdExample.description: Placeholder text inside the GitLab Application ID field showing an example token-like value.

admin.gitlab.clientIdTitle.description: Setting label for a text field in the GitLab OAuth admin settings; Application ID is GitLab terminology for the OAuth client ID. Ends with a colon.

admin.gitlab.clientSecretDescription.defaultMessage: Obtain this value via the instructions above for logging into GitLab.
admin.gitlab.clientSecretDescription.description: Admin console help text under the GitLab Application Secret Key field; the instructions above refers to the numbered GitLab setup steps on the same page.

admin.gitlab.clientSecretExample.description: Placeholder text inside the GitLab Application Secret Key field showing an example token-like value.

admin.gitlab.clientSecretTitle.description: Setting label for a text field in the GitLab OAuth admin settings; Application Secret Key is GitLab terminology for the OAuth client secret. Ends with a colon.

admin.gitlab.discoveryEndpointDesc.defaultMessage: The URL of the discovery document for OpenID Connect with GitLab.
admin.gitlab.discoveryEndpointDesc.description: Admin console help text under the Discovery Endpoint field in the GitLab OpenID Connect settings.

admin.gitlab.EnableMarkdownDesc.defaultMessage:
1. Log in to your GitLab account and go to Profile Settings -> Applications.
2. Enter Redirect URIs "<loginUrlChunk>your-mattermost-url</loginUrlChunk>" (example: http://localhost:8065/login/gitlab/complete) and "<signupUrlChunk>your-mattermost-url</signupUrlChunk>".
3. Then use "Application Secret Key" and "Application ID" fields from GitLab to complete the options below.
4. Complete the Endpoint URLs below.
admin.gitlab.EnableMarkdownDesc.description: Numbered step-by-step setup instructions shown under the GitLab option on the OAuth/OpenID admin page; loginUrlChunk and signupUrlChunk tags are replaced with URL templates at runtime, so keep the your-mattermost-url text inside them.

admin.gitlab.siteUrl.description: Setting label for a text field in the GitLab authentication admin settings; the base URL of the admin's GitLab instance. Ends with a colon.

admin.gitlab.siteUrlDescription.defaultMessage: Enter the URL of your GitLab instance, e.g. https://example.com:3000. If your GitLab instance is not set up with SSL, start the URL with http:// instead of https://.
admin.gitlab.siteUrlDescription.description: Help text for the GitLab Site URL setting in the System Console GitLab authentication page.

admin.gitlab.siteUrlExample.description: Placeholder example for the GitLab Site URL input, showing the URL prefix format.

admin.gitlab.tokenTitle.description: Setting label for a text field in the GitLab OAuth admin settings; the OAuth token endpoint URL. Ends with a colon.

admin.gitlab.userTitle.description: Setting label for a text field in the GitLab OAuth admin settings; the API endpoint used to fetch the user profile. Ends with a colon.

admin.global_attributes.applies_to.add_r.description: Button (verb phrase) in the 'Applies to' card on the Classification attribute page in the System Console, shown when the attribute is not yet applied to any resource; adds the Channels resource. 'Resource' means an object type such as channels.

admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.defaultMessage: Can be changed at any time
admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.description: Menu option and selected-value label for the 'Changing the value' setting in an attribute's Channels settings (System Console attribute pages). Means channel admins can change the channel's attribute value freely after it is set.

Screen-reader label for the 'Changing the value' dropdown button in an attribute's Channels settings in the System Console. {value} is the currently selected policy label, e.g. 'Can be changed at any time'.

Field label (noun phrase, i.e. 'how the value may be changed') for the dropdown that sets whether a channel's value for this attribute can later be changed, raised, or lowered. Shown in the Channels settings of an attribute in the System Console.

admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.defaultMessage: Can only be lowered, never raised
admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.description: Menu option for the 'Changing the value' setting in an attribute's Channels settings in the System Console. Only offered for Rank attributes, whose values are ordered: once set, a channel's value may move down the ranking but never up.
Menu option for the 'Changing the value' setting in an attribute's Channels settings in the System Console: the channel's value is locked once it has been set.

admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.defaultMessage: Can only be raised, never lowered
admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.description: Menu option for the 'Changing the value' setting in an attribute's Channels settings in the System Console. Only offered for Rank attributes, whose values are ordered: once set, a channel's value may move up the ranking but never down.

admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.defaultMessage: Raising and lowering need ranked values, so they are only offered on a Rank attribute.
admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.description: Help text under the 'Changing the value' dropdown in an attribute's Channels settings, shown for non-Rank attributes to explain why the raise-only/lower-only options are missing. 'Rank' is the name of an attribute type; translate it consistently with the type selector.
Screen-reader label for the chevron button that collapses the Channels row in an attribute's 'Applies to' card in the System Console.

admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.defaultMessage: Multiple display locations can be selected. You can always view and set the attribute value in the Channel Info sidebar. Unset values do not appear in the channel.
admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.description: Help text under the 'Display location' checkboxes in an attribute's Channels settings in the System Console. 'display locations' are the Header, Channel Info and Banner checkbox options, and 'Channel Info sidebar' is the Channel Info side panel in the channel view; use the same translation as the Channel Info option. 'Unset values' are channels that have no value for this attribute.

Field label for a group of checkboxes (Header, Channel Info, Banner) that choose where a channel's value for this attribute is shown to users. Shown in an attribute's Channels settings in the System Console.
Screen-reader label for the chevron button that expands the Channels row in an attribute's 'Applies to' card in the System Console.
Checkbox option under 'Display location' in an attribute's Channels settings, and a segment of the collapsed row summary: shows the attribute value in the banner at the top of the channel.
Checkbox option under 'Display location' in an attribute's Channels settings, and a segment of the collapsed row summary: shows the attribute value in the channel header.

Checkbox option under 'Display location' in an attribute's Channels settings, and a segment of the collapsed row summary. Refers to the Channel Info side panel in the channel view; it is a localized UI name, so match the translation used for that panel.

Stands in for the attribute's name in the System Console > Attribute Management > attribute details, Channels "Applies to" row, Required-toggle banner text when the attribute has no display name yet; used inside a sentence, so keep it lowercase.

admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.defaultMessage: {count, plural, one {# channel doesn't} other {# channels don't}} have a {attribute} value yet. Set a value on every existing channel before turning Required on.
admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.description: Body of the System Console > Attribute Management > attribute details, Channels "Applies to" row, Required-toggle banner, shown while Required is off and some channels have no value; {attribute} is the attribute's name. Required can only be turned on once every existing channel has a value.

admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.defaultMessage: {count, plural, one {# channel doesn't} other {# channels don't}} have a {attribute} value yet. New channels must set one; existing channels keep working until a value is set.
admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.description: Body of the System Console > Attribute Management > attribute details, Channels "Applies to" row, Required-toggle banner, shown when the attribute is already Required but some channels still have no value; {attribute} is the attribute's name.

admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.defaultMessage: Save this attribute first, then set a value on every existing channel before turning Required on.
admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.description: Body of the System Console > Attribute Management > attribute details, Channels "Applies to" row, Required-toggle banner, shown while the attribute is still being created and has not been saved yet.

Button in the System Console > Attribute Management > attribute details, Channels "Applies to" row, Required-toggle banner that sends a direct-message reminder to every admin of a channel missing a value.

admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.defaultMessage: The notifications couldn't be sent. Please try again.
admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.description: Error message in the System Console > Attribute Management > attribute details, Channels "Applies to" row, Required-toggle banner when sending the reminders to channel admins failed.

admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.defaultMessage: Notification queued for {count, plural, one {# channel admin} other {# channel admins}}.
admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.description: Success message in the System Console > Attribute Management > attribute details, Channels "Applies to" row, Required-toggle banner after reminders were queued for background delivery; {count} is the number of channel admins queued to receive a reminder.

admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.defaultMessage: Notification queued for {count, plural, one {# channel admin} other {# channel admins}}. Some channel admins were not reached because this attribute affects more admins than one run can notify. Use View channel list to see the channels still missing a value.
admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.description: Warning message in the System Console > Attribute Management > attribute details, Channels "Applies to" row, Required-toggle banner after reminders were queued but not every channel admin could be reached in one run; {count} is the number queued. "View channel list" is the label of the banner's other button, which lists the channels still missing a value.
Title of the System Console > Attribute Management > attribute details, Channels "Applies to" row, Required-toggle banner, which warns that some channels have no value for this attribute.
Link in the System Console > Attribute Management > attribute details, Channels "Applies to" row, Required-toggle banner that opens the list of channels with no value for this attribute.
Destructive button in the expanded Channels row of an attribute's 'Applies to' card in the System Console; stops the attribute from applying to channels.

admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.defaultMessage: Optional — this attribute can still be added to a channel after it is created.
admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.description: Help text under the Required toggle in an attribute's Channels settings, shown when the toggle is off. The leading word restates the state (optional) and is followed by an explanation.

admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.defaultMessage: Required — the channel must have a value for this attribute before it can be created.
admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.description: Help text under the Required toggle in an attribute's Channels settings, shown when the toggle is on. The leading word restates the state and is followed by an explanation of what it enforces on channel creation.

Field label (adjective) for the toggle that makes a value for this attribute mandatory when creating a channel, in an attribute's Channels settings in the System Console. Also used as the toggle's screen-reader label.

Segment of the one-line summary on the collapsed/header Channels row of an attribute's 'Applies to' settings, e.g. 'Optional · Display: Header + Channel Info'. {locations} is the already-translated display location names joined with ' + '.

Segment of the one-line summary on the Channels row of an attribute's 'Applies to' settings, shown when no display location is checked: the value appears only in the Channel Info side panel (localized panel name).
Short segment of the one-line summary on the Channels row of an attribute's 'Applies to' settings, meaning the change policy is 'can only be lowered, never raised' (Rank attributes). Keep it brief.
Short segment of the one-line summary on the Channels row of an attribute's 'Applies to' settings, meaning the channel's value cannot be changed after it is first set. Keep it brief.
First segment (adjective) of the one-line summary on the Channels row of an attribute's 'Applies to' settings, meaning a value for this attribute is not required when creating a channel.
Short segment of the one-line summary on the Channels row of an attribute's 'Applies to' settings, meaning the change policy is 'can only be raised, never lowered' (Rank attributes). Keep it brief.
First segment (adjective) of the one-line summary on the Channels row of an attribute's 'Applies to' settings, meaning channels must have a value for this attribute when created.
Heading of the Channels row in an attribute's 'Applies to' card in the System Console; names the resource type (channels) the attribute applies to.
State text shown next to the Required toggle switch in an attribute's Channels settings when the switch is off.
State text shown next to the Required toggle switch in an attribute's Channels settings when the switch is on.
Button that closes the System Console "Channels without a value" modal, opened from the Required banner of a channel attribute.
Column header in the System Console "Channels without a value" modal, opened from the Required banner of a channel attribute for the channel admins of each listed channel.
Column header in the System Console "Channels without a value" modal, opened from the Required banner of a channel attribute for the channel name.
Empty state of the System Console "Channels without a value" modal, opened from the Required banner of a channel attribute when no channel is missing a value anymore.

admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.defaultMessage: No matching channels on this page
admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.description: Empty state of the System Console "Channels without a value" modal, shown when the selected Local or Shared filter matches no channel on the current page although other pages still have channels missing a value.

admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.defaultMessage: The channel list couldn't be loaded.
admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.description: Error message in the System Console "Channels without a value" modal, opened from the Required banner of a channel attribute when the list of channels failed to load.
Filter tab in the System Console "Channels without a value" modal, opened from the Required banner of a channel attribute showing every channel; {count} is the number of channels.

Filter tab in the System Console "Channels without a value" modal, opened from the Required banner of a channel attribute showing only this server's own channels, not shared ones; {count} is the number of channels.

Filter tab in the System Console "Channels without a value" modal, opened from the Required banner of a channel attribute showing only channels shared from another server (shared channels); {count} is the number of channels.
Pagination button for the next page of the System Console "Channels without a value" modal, opened from the Required banner of a channel attribute.
Shown in the Channel admin column of the System Console "Channels without a value" modal, opened from the Required banner of a channel attribute when a channel has no channel admin.

Accessible label for the link that opens a listed channel in a new browser tab, in the System Console "Channels without a value" modal, opened from the Required banner of a channel attribute; {channel} is the channel's name.
Pagination button for the previous page of the System Console "Channels without a value" modal, opened from the Required banner of a channel attribute.
Button in the System Console "Channels without a value" modal, opened from the Required banner of a channel attribute that retries loading the channel list after an error.

admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.defaultMessage: {count, plural, one {# channel} other {# channels}} still need a {attribute} value
admin.global_attributes.applies_to.chann.description: Subtitle of the System Console "Channels without a value" modal, opened from the Required banner of a channel attribute; {count} is the number of channels with no value and {attribute} is the attribute's name.
Title of the System Console "Channels without a value" modal, opened from the Required banner of a channel attribute, which lists the channels that have no value for the attribute.

admin.global_attributes.applies_to.empty.defaultMessage: This attribute does not apply to any resource yet.
admin.global_attributes.applies_to.empty.description: Empty-state message in the 'Applies to' card on the Classification attribute page in the System Console, shown when the attribute is not applied to channels or any other resource type.

admin.global_attributes.applies_to.read_.description: Read-only row in the 'Applies to' card on the Classification attribute page in the System Console, naming a resource this page does not edit. {resource} is a resource name such as Users; {name} is the unique name of the attribute created for it, which policies refer to.

admin.global_attributes.applies_to.subti.defaultMessage: Resources this attribute applies to, and how it behaves on each.
admin.global_attributes.applies_to.subti.description: Subtitle under the 'Applies to' card heading on the Classification attribute page in the System Console. 'Resources' means object types such as channels.

admin.global_attributes.applies_to.title.description: Heading of the card on the Classification attribute page in the System Console that lists which resource types (such as channels) the attribute applies to.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Label of the button in the header of the 'Applies to' card on the System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management attribute detail page, which opens a menu of resource types. 'Add' is a verb; also used as the button's accessible label.
Label of the same add button when it is rendered below an existing list of resources on the attribute detail page. 'Add' is a verb; 'another' signals that at least one resource is already listed.
Heading of the empty state inside the 'Applies to' card on the attribute detail page, shown before any resource type has been added.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Add a resource to apply this attribute to users, channels, or posts.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Helper sentence under that empty-state heading, telling the admin what to do next. 'users, channels, or posts' are the three resource types this attribute can be attached to.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Resources for plugin-managed attributes can't be added here.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Empty-state helper text in the Applies-to section of the attribute details page in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management for an attribute a plugin owns, where resources cannot be added.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: No additional settings for this resource yet.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Placeholder text inside an expanded resource row of the 'Applies to' card, shown because per-resource settings are not implemented yet.

Accessible label (aria-label) of the toggle button on an expanded resource row in the 'Applies to' card. {label} is the resource type name — 'Users', 'Channels' or 'Posts'. 'Collapse' is an imperative verb.

Accessible label (aria-label) of the toggle button on a collapsed resource row in the 'Applies to' card. {label} is the resource type name — 'Users', 'Channels' or 'Posts'. 'Expand' is an imperative verb.
Label of the destructive button inside an expanded resource row of the 'Applies to' card, which detaches that resource type from the attribute. 'Remove' is a verb.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Managed by: {value}. Values are synced from an external source and cannot be changed here.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Screen-reader label for the locked 'Managed by' field in the Users row of an attribute's 'Applies to' section (System Console > Attribute Management > attribute details). {value} is the external source name, e.g. 'AD/LDAP' or 'SAML'.

Help text under the locked 'Managed by' field in the Users row of an attribute's 'Applies to' section, shown when user values are synced from AD/LDAP or SAML. 'Mattermost' is the product name and is not translated.
Field label in the Users row of an attribute's 'Applies to' section (System Console > Attribute Management > attribute details), next to a locked field naming the external sync source (e.g. AD/LDAP).
Segmented-button option for 'Profile display' in the Users row of an attribute's 'Applies to' section: the attribute is always shown on user profiles, even when empty.
Segmented-button option for 'Profile display' in the Users row of an attribute's 'Applies to' section: the attribute is never shown on user profiles.

Field label (noun phrase) for the segmented control (Always / When set / Hidden) that controls whether the attribute is shown on user profiles. In the Users row of an attribute's 'Applies to' section in the System Console.
Segmented-button option for 'Profile display' in the Users row of an attribute's 'Applies to' section: the attribute is shown on a user's profile only if that user has a value.

Radio option under 'Who can set the value' in the Users row of an attribute's 'Applies to' section: only system admins can set users' values. Refers to the System Administrator role; use the standard translation of that role name.

Help text under the 'Who can set the value' radio options in the Users row of an attribute's 'Applies to' section. 'Member' and 'System Administrator' are the two option labels; use the same translations.

Field label for the radio group that chooses whether users edit their own value for this attribute or only system admins can. In the Users row of an attribute's 'Applies to' section in the System Console.
Radio option under 'Who can set the value' in the Users row of an attribute's 'Applies to' section: each user (a regular member) can set their own value. Noun, singular.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: This resource cannot be changed — this attribute was managed by a plugin that's no longer installed.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Tooltip on a locked Applies-to resource in the attribute details page in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management whose managing plugin is no longer installed.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: This resource cannot be changed — this attribute is managed by a plugin.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Tooltip on a locked Applies-to resource in the attribute details page in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management, explaining a plugin manages the attribute.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: This resource cannot be changed — this attribute applies to only one resource.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Tooltip on the disabled row in an attribute's 'Applies to' list (System Console > Attribute Management > attribute details), explaining that the only resource type (e.g. Users) cannot be removed or changed because it is the attribute's sole one.

Tooltip on the locked Users row in an attribute's "Applies to" list (System Console > Attribute Management > attribute details), shown while integrations own the attribute so the Users resource cannot be removed. {owners} is a localized list of the integrations that own the attribute (for example "SCIM and svc-sync").
Name of the 'channel' resource type on the attribute detail page — used as a menu item in the add-resource picker and as the label of the corresponding row. Plural noun.
Name of the 'post' resource type on the attribute detail page — used as a menu item in the add-resource picker and as the label of the corresponding row. Plural noun ('post' as in a chat message).
Name of the 'user' resource type on the attribute detail page — used as a menu item in the add-resource picker and as the label of the corresponding row. Plural noun.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Resources this attribute applies to, and who can set the value on each.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Subtitle under the 'Applies to' card heading on the attribute detail page, describing what the card contains. 'Resources' means users, channels and posts.
Heading of the card on the attribute detail page listing which resource types the attribute is attached to. A short noun phrase, not a sentence.

Text of the breadcrumb-style back link at the top of the attribute detail page, returning to System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management. 'Attribute Management' is the name of that page and should match its sidebar label.
Label of the Cancel button in the save bar of the attribute detail page, discarding unsaved changes. Verb.
Subtitle under the 'Definition' card heading on the attribute detail page, listing the fields the card contains. A fragment, not a sentence.
Heading of the first card on the attribute detail page, holding the display name, type and options fields. A noun.
Label of the text input for the attribute's human-readable name on the attribute detail page. Contrasted with the internal 'unique name' shown beneath it.
Placeholder text inside the empty display name input on the attribute detail page. 'Add' is an imperative verb.

Page heading (h1) of the attribute details page in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management when editing an existing attribute, as opposed to creating one; {name} is the attribute's name.

Text of the chip shown on the attribute detail page for an attribute linked to an external directory. {source} is the source name ('AD/LDAP' or 'SAML') and {value} is the external attribute name it syncs from. Keep the separator format.

Second line of a disabled entry in the 'Link to external source' menu on the attribute detail page. {sources} lists the already-linked identity sources (AD/LDAP, SAML, OpenID Connect) that this source cannot be combined with.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: An attribute synced from OpenID Connect can't also sync from AD/LDAP or SAML. Remove the {sources} {count, plural, one {link} other {links}} to link {source}.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Tooltip on a disabled entry in the 'Link to external source' menu. {sources} lists the linked identity sources to remove, {count} is how many there are, and {source} is the source the admin wanted to link. AD/LDAP, SAML and OpenID Connect are product names.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Cannot link an external source while this attribute applies to a resource.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Tooltip on the disabled external-source control in the attribute details page in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management, explaining it cannot be linked while the attribute applies to a resource.

Accessible label (aria-label) of the pencil button on an external source chip on the attribute detail page. {source} is 'AD/LDAP' or 'SAML'. 'Edit' is a verb and 'link' is a noun meaning the configured mapping.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: The attribute in your AD/LDAP directory to sync this value from.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Help text inside the 'Link to AD/LDAP' modal on the attribute detail page, above the input where the admin types the AD/LDAP attribute name to sync from.
Header of the modal opened from the 'Link to external source' menu on the attribute detail page when AD/LDAP is chosen. 'Link' is a verb here.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Sync with your directory of record
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Second line of the AD/LDAP item in the 'Link to external source' dropdown on the attribute detail page. 'Directory of record' means the authoritative AD/LDAP directory.

Primary label of the AD/LDAP item in the 'Link to external source' dropdown on the attribute detail page, also reused inside the chip and its button labels. A product/protocol name — keep it in English.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: {count, plural, one {External source link removed} other {External source links removed}}
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Screen-reader-only status announcement on the attribute detail page after changing the attribute Type clears its external source link(s). {count} is how many links were cleared; the message names no source, only the number.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: The claim in the ID token or userinfo response to sync this value from, for example department. Use dots for nested claims, such as address.country. If the claim is missing at sign-in, the value is removed.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Help text in the 'Link to OpenID Connect' dialog on the attribute detail page, under the field where the admin types a claim name. 'ID token' and 'userinfo' are OpenID Connect terms; department and address.country are literal example claim names and should stay as-is.
Title of the dialog where an admin types the OpenID Connect claim an attribute is synced from. 'OpenID Connect' is a protocol name.
Second line of the OpenID Connect entry in the 'Link to external source' menu, describing that values come from OpenID Connect claims when users sign in.
Name of the OpenID Connect identity source in the 'Link to external source' menu, its link chip and the attributes table. Protocol name; usually left untranslated.

Accessible label (aria-label) of the X button on an external source chip on the attribute detail page. {source} is 'AD/LDAP' or 'SAML'. 'Remove' is a verb and 'link' is a noun meaning the configured mapping.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: The attribute in your SAML response to sync this value from.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Help text inside the 'Link to SAML' modal on the attribute detail page, above the input where the admin types the SAML assertion attribute name to sync from.
Header of the modal opened from the 'Link to external source' menu on the attribute detail page when SAML is chosen. 'Link' is a verb here.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Map values from SAML at sign-in
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Second line of the SAML item in the 'Link to external source' dropdown on the attribute detail page. Explains that the value is taken from the SAML response when the user signs in.
Primary label of the SAML item in the 'Link to external source' dropdown on the attribute detail page, also reused inside the chip and its button labels. A protocol acronym — keep it in English.

Static label shown to the left of the external source chips on the attribute detail page, introducing the list of linked sources. A fragment ending in a preposition — treat as 'Synced with:' and adapt to the target language's word order.
Label of the dropdown button on the attribute detail page that opens the AD/LDAP and SAML choices. 'Link' is a verb here.
Second line of the disabled OpenID Connect entry in the 'Link to external source' menu when the server has turned this feature off.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Syncing attributes from {source} is turned off on this server.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Tooltip on the disabled OpenID Connect entry in the 'Link to external source' menu when the server has turned this feature off. {source} is the source name, OpenID Connect.
Second line of the disabled OpenID Connect entry in the 'Link to external source' menu when OpenID Connect sign-in is not set up yet. {source} is the source name, OpenID Connect.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Turn on {source} in System Console > Authentication > {source} to link attributes to its claims.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Tooltip on the disabled OpenID Connect entry in the 'Link to external source' menu when OpenID Connect sign-in is off. {source} is OpenID Connect; 'System Console > Authentication > {source}' is the navigation path to its settings page and should match those menu names.
Second line of the disabled OpenID Connect entry in the 'Link to external source' menu when the license does not include OpenID Connect.
Tooltip on the disabled OpenID Connect entry in the 'Link to external source' menu when the license does not include it. {source} is the source name, OpenID Connect.

Confirm button in the 'Can't delete' dialog for a value of a hierarchical attribute in the System Console. {name} is the name of the first child value that would be left without a parent; clicking jumps to it in the list.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: {count, plural, one {Child values need a parent. {name} is the only parent of 1 child value, so it can't be deleted until that child is moved or deleted.} other {Child values need a parent. {name} is the only parent of {count} child values, so it can't be deleted until those children are moved or deleted.}}
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Body of the dialog shown when an admin tries to delete a value of a hierarchical attribute that is the only parent of other values. {name} is the value being deleted (shown in bold); {count} is how many child values would be left without a parent.
Title of the dialog shown when a value of a hierarchical attribute cannot be deleted because some child values have no other parent. {name} is the admin-defined value name.
Destructive confirm button (verb) in the 'Delete value?' dialog for a value of a hierarchical attribute in the System Console.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: {count, plural, one {1 child ({children}) of this value has other parent values, so it will not be removed. Are you sure you want to delete {name}?} other {{count} children ({children}) of this value have other parent values, so they will not be removed. Are you sure you want to delete {name}?}}
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Body of the confirmation dialog when deleting a value of a hierarchical attribute whose children also have other parents. {count} is the number of direct child values; {children} is their names joined as a list; {name} is the value being deleted (bold).
Title of the confirmation dialog for deleting a value of a hierarchical attribute in the System Console. {name} is the admin-defined value name.
Confirm button (verb) in the dialog that confirms adding a parent to a value of a hierarchical attribute in the System Console.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: {child} and all of its child values will also sit under {parent}. Are you sure you want to add this parent?
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Body of the confirmation dialog shown when adding a parent to a value of a hierarchical attribute would bring more values under that parent. {child} is the value gaining the parent; {parent} is the new parent value (both admin-defined names, shown bold).
Title of the confirmation dialog shown when an admin adds a parent to a value of a hierarchical attribute. {parent} is the admin-defined name of the value that would become the parent.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Name must start with a letter or underscore, and contain only letters, numbers, and underscores.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Inline validation error under the unique name field on the attribute detail page when the typed name uses disallowed characters. Describes the allowed character set to a system admin.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: "{word}" is a reserved word and cannot be used as a name.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Inline validation error under the unique name field on the attribute detail page. {word} is the reserved identifier the admin typed; keep it inside quotes and untranslated.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Name must be {max} characters or fewer.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Inline validation error under the unique name field on the attribute detail page. {max} is the maximum allowed number of characters.
Placeholder text of the input where an admin types new option values for a select-type attribute on the attribute detail page. '(required)' marks the field as mandatory; keep the ellipsis character.
Accessible label (aria-label) of the popover that opens when an option chip is clicked on the attribute detail page. 'Edit' is a verb, 'option' is one value of a select-type attribute.
Button (verb) that saves a new child value typed into the inline form under a row in the value hierarchy editor of an attribute details page in the System Console.
Tooltip and screen-reader label for the plus icon button on a row of the value hierarchy editor; adds a new child value. {name} is the row's value name.
Placeholder and label of the input at the bottom of the value hierarchy editor for adding a new value with no parent (at the root of the hierarchy).
Button (verb phrase) next to the new-value input in the value hierarchy editor of an attribute details page; adds the typed value at the top level.
Button (verb) that closes the inline new-child-value form in the value hierarchy editor without adding anything.
Screen-reader label for the inline input that names a new child value in the value hierarchy editor. {name} is the parent value; 'granted by' means the new value sits under that parent.
Placeholder of the inline input for naming a new child value under a row in the value hierarchy editor (imperative).
Screen-reader label for the chevron button that hides the child values of a row in the value hierarchy editor. {name} is the row's value name.
Tooltip and screen-reader label for the trash icon button on a row of the value hierarchy editor. {name} is the value to delete.
Destructive item in the per-value menu of the value hierarchy editor (opened from a row) that deletes the value.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Drop on a row to nest it under that value. Order in the list carries no meaning.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Hint for the drag handle on each row of the value hierarchy editor, explaining that dropping a value onto another row makes it a child of that row, and that list order is not significant.
Tooltip on the drag handle of a row in the value hierarchy editor. {name} is the value being dragged.
Inline error in the value hierarchy editor when a typed value name matches an existing value of this attribute. {name} is the typed name; 'field' means this attribute.
Label for the action that renames or edits a value on a row of the value hierarchy editor. {name} is the row's value name.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Start with a top-level value. You can add parents and children from its row.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Body text of the empty state of the value hierarchy editor (hierarchical attribute with no values yet), above the first-value input.
Heading of the empty state of the value hierarchy editor, shown when a hierarchical attribute has no values yet (imperative).
Screen-reader label for the chevron button that shows the child values of a row in the value hierarchy editor. {name} is the row's value name.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Up to 100 parents per value, 100 levels deep.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Footer note under the value hierarchy editor stating the limits: each value can have at most 100 parents and the hierarchy can be at most 100 levels deep.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Each value can have parents and children.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Helper text above the value hierarchy editor for a hierarchical attribute on its System Console details page.
Placeholder of the input for the first value when the value hierarchy editor is empty.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: {parent} can't be a parent of {child} — {child} already grants {parent}, so this would loop back on itself.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Error shown in the value hierarchy editor when an admin tries to make {parent} a parent of {child} although {child} is already an ancestor of {parent}. Both are admin-defined value names; 'grants' means 'is above in the hierarchy'.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Adding this parent pushes "{name}" to depth {n}; the limit is 100.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Error shown in the value hierarchy editor when adding a parent would make the hierarchy too deep. {name} is the affected value; {n} is the depth (number of levels) it would reach.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: An option can have at most 100 parents.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Error shown in the value hierarchy editor when an admin tries to give a value more than 100 parents. 'Option' means a value of the attribute.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Parents — who this value is granted by
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Tooltip on the icon button on a row of the value hierarchy editor that opens the list of parents for that value, i.e. the values above it.
Screen-reader label for the icon button on a row of the value hierarchy editor that opens its parents list. {name} is the row's value name.
Badge on a row of the value hierarchy editor, shown only when the value has two or more parents. {n} is the parent count (always 2 or more).
Tooltip on the parent-count badge of a row in the value hierarchy editor. {names} is the list of parent value names, already joined into a list (e.g. 'A, B, and C').

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Add a child, or type a new name…
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Placeholder of the search input in a value's Children panel (hierarchy editor menu); picks an existing value or creates a new one as a child.
Screen-reader label for the search input in a value's Children panel. {name} is the value that will become the parent of the added value.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Add a parent, or type a new name…
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Placeholder of the search input in a value's Parents panel (hierarchy editor menu); picks an existing value or creates a new one as a parent.
Screen-reader label for the search input in a value's Parents panel. {name} is the value that will receive the new parent.
Back button heading the Parents panel in a value's menu in the value hierarchy editor. {name} is the value whose parents are listed.
Menu item (noun, plural) in a value's menu in the value hierarchy editor that opens the list of its child values; the count or 'None' is shown beside it.
Back button heading the Children panel in a value's menu in the value hierarchy editor. {name} is the value whose children are listed.
Suggestion button in the Parents or Children search list of the value hierarchy editor, offered when the typed name does not exist; creates a new value with that name. {name} is the typed text.
Empty-state text in a value's Children panel of the value hierarchy editor.
Empty-state text in a value's Parents panel of the value hierarchy editor.
Count shown beside the Children item in a value's menu in the value hierarchy editor when the value has no children (stands in for zero).
Count shown beside the Parents item in a value's menu in the value hierarchy editor. {n} is the number of parent values (1 or more).
Menu item (noun, plural) in a value's menu in the value hierarchy editor that opens the list of its parent values; the count or 'Top level' is shown beside it.
Screen-reader label for the remove button next to a child in a value's Children panel. {child} is the child value; {parent} is the value whose panel is open.
Screen-reader label for the remove button next to a parent in a value's Parents panel. {parent} is the parent value; {child} is the value whose panel is open.

Tooltip on the remove (X) icon next to each parent in the Parents list of a hierarchical attribute's value editor, in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management. 'Remove' is a verb; 'Parent' means a parent value in the hierarchy.

Shown in the Parents row of a hierarchical attribute's value editor (System Console > Attribute Management) when the selected value has no parents, meaning it sits at the root of the hierarchy. Replaces the parent count.
Screen-reader label for the text input where an admin renames the selected value of a hierarchical attribute, in System Console > Attribute Management. 'Name' is a noun.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Text attributes have no preset values — a value is typed in per resource.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Help text shown under the Options area on the attribute detail page when the attribute Type is Text, explaining why there are no options to configure. The em dash separates two clauses.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: There's a problem with one or more options — check for a duplicate or overly long name, or a missing/duplicate rank.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Inline validation error shown under the Options area on the attribute detail page when one or more option chips are malformed. 'Rank' refers to the ordering number on ranked options.
Label of the Options field on the attribute detail page, above the list of option chips for a select-type attribute. Plural noun.
Placeholder text of the text input inside an option chip's edit popover on the attribute detail page, where the option's display text is typed.
Label of the submenu inside an unranked option chip's edit popover on the attribute detail page, used to reorder the option in the list. 'Move' is a verb.

Suffix shown next to the rank number of the top-ranked option in a ranked attribute's chip menu on the attribute detail page. {rank} is the numeric rank; '(Highest)' marks it as the highest of the set.

Suffix shown next to the rank number of the bottom-ranked option in a ranked attribute's chip menu on the attribute detail page. {rank} is the numeric rank; '(Lowest)' marks it as the lowest of the set.
Label of the submenu inside a ranked option chip's edit popover on the attribute detail page, used to change that option's rank. A noun.
Accessible label (aria-label) of the X button on an option chip on the attribute detail page, deleting that option. 'Remove' is a verb.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: At least one option is required.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Inline validation error under the Options field on the attribute detail page when a select-type attribute has no options defined.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Options are managed by the {source} sync. Each value it sends is added as an option, and options that no user holds any more are removed.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Shown under the read-only option list of a select or multiselect attribute linked to an identity source. {source} is the source name, such as AD/LDAP or SAML; the sync creates and removes the options, so the admin cannot edit them.
Accessible name of the read-only list of option chips on a synced select or multiselect attribute's detail page. Plural noun.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Add Users under Applies to. The {source} sync creates these options from the values it syncs to users.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Inline error under the read-only options of a select or multiselect attribute linked to an external source while the attribute does not apply to Users, which keeps it from being saved. "Users" and "Applies to" are the labels of the resource and the card on the same page. {source} is the external source name, such as AD/LDAP or SAML.
Inline validation error shown while editing or adding an option value on the attribute detail page, when the typed value duplicates an existing option.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Values for users are set by {owners}. Unique name and type are locked; display name, options, and Profile display can still be changed here.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Helper text under the "Managed by" note on the attribute details page in System Console > Attribute Management, for an attribute owned by integrations. Explains which fields are locked and which can still be edited. {owners} is a localized list of the integrations that own the attribute (for example "SCIM and svc-sync"). "Profile display" is the name of a setting on the same page.

Note at the top of the attribute details page in System Console > Attribute Management, naming the integrations that own the attribute and set its user values. {owners} is a localized list of the integrations that own the attribute (for example "SCIM and svc-sync").
Link next to the "Managed by" note on the attribute details page in System Console > Attribute Management that opens the owning plugin's settings page. {pluginName} is the plugin's display name.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Name, type, and values are owned by the plugin and are read-only here.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Helper text in the attribute details page in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management for a plugin-owned attribute, explaining which fields are read-only.
Label in the attribute details page in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management naming the plugin that owns the attribute.
Label in the attribute details page in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management naming the plugin that owned the attribute, where that plugin is no longer installed.
Link in the attribute details page in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management to the settings page of the plugin that owns the attribute.
Label of the Save button in the save bar of the attribute detail page. Verb.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: The attribute was saved, but its {resources} settings (Profile display, Who can set the value) couldn't be updated. Please try again.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Error banner on the attribute edit page in System Console > Attribute Management, shown when the attribute saved but its per-resource settings did not. {resources} is a localized list of resource types such as 'Users' or 'Channels'. 'Profile display' and 'Who can set the value' are setting labels on the same page and must match their translations.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: The attribute was saved, but its {resources} display name couldn't be updated. Please try again.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Error banner on the attribute edit page in System Console > Attribute Management, shown when the attribute saved but its display name for a resource type did not update. {resources} is a localized list of resource types such as 'Users' or 'Channels'.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Couldn't apply this attribute to {resources}. Nothing was saved — please try again.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Error banner on the attribute detail page after saving failed while attaching the attribute to resources. {resources} is a localized, comma-joined list of resource type names such as 'Users, Channels'. Reassures the admin that nothing was persisted.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: The maximum number of User Attributes has been reached. Delete an existing one before applying this attribute to Users.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Error banner on the attribute detail page when the attribute cannot be applied to Users because the server's cap on User Attributes is already reached. 'User Attributes' is the name of the related System Console feature.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: This name is already used by a User Attribute. Please choose a different name.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Error banner on the attribute detail page when the attribute's name collides with an existing User Attribute (a separate System Console feature that shares the same name space).

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: The attribute was saved, but couldn't be applied to {resources}. Please try again.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Error in the attribute details page in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management when the attribute saved but could not be applied to some resources. {resources} is a list of resource names.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Couldn't remove this attribute from {resources}. Nothing else was saved — please try again.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Error in the attribute details page in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management when removing the attribute from resources failed and nothing was saved. {resources} is a list of resource names.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: The attribute was saved, but couldn't be removed from {resources}. Please try again.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Error in the attribute details page in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management when the attribute saved but could not be removed from some resources. {resources} is a list of resource names.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: "{name}" may have been partially created for {resources}. A retry under the same name will likely fail until those are cleaned up.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Red error banner on the System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management > New attribute page, shown when saving partly succeeded and the automatic cleanup also failed. {name} is the attribute's display name as typed by the admin; {resources} is a comma-separated list of already-localized resource-type labels (e.g. "Users, Channels").

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: "{name}" was created but could not be cleaned up after a failed apply. A retry under the same name will likely fail until it is deleted.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Red error banner on the System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management > New attribute page. Variant of the rollback-failed message used when no resource types are left to name; {name} is the attribute's display name as typed by the admin.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: The attribute was created, but it could not be applied to channels. Its definition can no longer be changed here; select Save to try applying it again, or remove the Channels resource to finish without it.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Error banner on the new-attribute page in System Console > Attribute Management, shown when the attribute was created but applying it to channels failed. 'Save' is the page's Save button and 'Channels' is the resource-type label on the same page; both should match their translations.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Something went wrong while saving this attribute. Please try again.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Fallback red error banner on the System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management > New attribute page when saving fails for an unrecognized reason.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Name must start with a letter or underscore, and contain only letters, numbers, and underscores.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Red error banner on the New attribute page (System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management) when the server rejects the attribute's unique name for using disallowed characters. "Name" here means the internal unique name, not the display name.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: There's a problem with one or more options — check for a duplicate or overly long name, or a missing/duplicate rank, then try again.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Red error banner on the New attribute page (System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management) when the server rejects the list of select/multiselect/ranked option values. "rank" is the numeric ordering position assigned to each option.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: You have reached the maximum number of attributes for this server. Delete an existing attribute before creating a new one.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Red error banner on the New attribute page (System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management) when the server's per-server cap on attribute definitions has been hit. Addressed to a system admin.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: An attribute with this name already exists. Please choose a different name.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Red error banner on the New attribute page (System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management) when another attribute already uses the same unique name.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: This name is a reserved word and cannot be used. Please choose a different name.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Red error banner on the New attribute page (System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management) when the chosen unique name matches a word reserved by the system.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: This attribute's type can't be changed while it applies to a resource. Remove those resources first, then try again.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Error in the attribute details page in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management when the attribute's type cannot change because it still applies to resources.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Add a display name, choose a type, and pick where it applies.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Subtitle line under the page heading of System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management > New attribute. Summarizes the three steps of the form below (display name, type, and which resources it applies to).
Page heading (h1) of the attribute creation page in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management. "New" is an adjective describing the attribute being created, not a verb.
Screen-reader label for the Type dropdown on the New attribute page. {value} is the currently selected, already-translated type name (Text, Select, Multiselect, Ranked, Other).

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Type: {value}. Locked while this attribute applies to a resource.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Screen-reader label for the locked Type field in the attribute details page in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management while the attribute applies to a resource. {value} is the current type.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Type: {value}. Locked while linked to an external source.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Screen-reader label for the locked Type field in the attribute details page in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management while the attribute is linked to AD/LDAP, SAML, or OpenID Connect. {value} is the current type.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Type: {value}. Locked because a hierarchical attribute cannot be converted to another type.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Screen-reader label for the disabled Type field on the attribute edit page in System Console > Attribute Management. {value} is the localized type name (for example 'Hierarchical'). Explains why a hierarchical attribute's type cannot be changed.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Type: {value}. Locked because this attribute is managed by {owners}.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Screen-reader label for the locked Type field on the attribute details page in System Console > Attribute Management, for an attribute owned by integrations. {value} is the current type. {owners} is a localized list of the integrations that own the attribute (for example "SCIM and svc-sync").

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Type: {value}. Locked because this attribute is managed by a plugin.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Screen-reader label for the locked Type field in the attribute details page in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management for an attribute a plugin manages. {value} is the current type.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Type: {value}. Locked because this attribute was managed by a plugin that's no longer installed.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Screen-reader label for the locked Type field in the attribute details page in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management whose managing plugin is no longer installed. {value} is the current type.
Form field label for the attribute type selector on the New attribute page (System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management). Noun.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Type cannot be changed while this attribute applies to a resource.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Tooltip on the locked Type field in the attribute details page in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management while the attribute applies to a resource.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Type cannot be changed while this attribute is linked to an external source.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Tooltip on the locked Type field in the attribute details page in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management while the attribute is linked to an external source.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Type cannot be changed — a hierarchical attribute cannot be converted to another type. Create a new attribute of the type you need instead.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Tooltip on the disabled Type field on the attribute edit page in System Console > Attribute Management, shown for hierarchical attributes. Explains why the type is locked and what the admin should do instead.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Type cannot be changed — this attribute is managed by {owners}.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Tooltip on the locked Type field on the attribute details page in System Console > Attribute Management, for an attribute owned by integrations. {owners} is a localized list of the integrations that own the attribute (for example "SCIM and svc-sync").

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Type cannot be changed — this attribute was managed by a plugin that's no longer installed.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Tooltip on the locked Type field in the attribute details page in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management whose managing plugin is no longer installed.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Type cannot be changed — this attribute is managed by a plugin.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Tooltip on the locked Type field in the attribute details page in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management for an attribute a plugin manages.
Accessible name for the dropdown menu that lists the available attribute types on the New attribute page. Imperative instruction to the admin.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Couldn't generate a unique name from this display name. Click Edit to set one manually.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Inline warning under the unique-name row on the New attribute page, shown when the display name the admin typed cannot be auto-converted into a valid unique name. "Edit" refers to the adjacent Edit link and should match its translation.
Text of the link that finishes inline editing of the unique name on the New attribute page. Pairs with the Edit link.
Screen-reader label for the Done link that finishes inline editing of the attribute's unique name on the New attribute page.
Text of the link that starts inline editing of the auto-generated unique name on the New attribute page. Verb.
Screen-reader label for the Edit link that starts inline editing of the attribute's unique name on the New attribute page.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Name is the internal identifier for policies and integrations. Display name is what admins and users see.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Helper paragraph under the display name / unique name fields on the New attribute page, explaining the difference between the two. "Name" refers to the unique internal identifier; "Display name" to the human-readable label.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Edit unique name. Locked while this attribute applies to a resource.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Screen-reader label for the locked name field in the attribute details page in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management while the attribute applies to a resource.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Name cannot be changed while this attribute applies to a resource. Remove and save first.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Tooltip on the locked name field in the attribute details page in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management while the attribute applies to a resource.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Edit unique name. Locked because this attribute is managed by {owners}.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Screen-reader label for the locked unique name field on the attribute details page in System Console > Attribute Management, for an attribute owned by integrations. {owners} is a localized list of the integrations that own the attribute (for example "SCIM and svc-sync").

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Name cannot be changed — this attribute is managed by {owners}.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Tooltip on the locked unique name field on the attribute details page in System Console > Attribute Management, for an attribute owned by integrations. {owners} is a localized list of the integrations that own the attribute (for example "SCIM and svc-sync").

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Edit unique name. Locked because this attribute is managed by a plugin.
admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.description: Screen-reader label for the locked name field in the attribute details page in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management for an attribute a plugin manages.

admin.global_attributes.attribute_detail.defaultMessage: Edit unique name. Locked because this attribute was managed by a plugin that's no longer installed.

admin.global_attributes.classification.b.description: Screen-reader label for the back-arrow link at the top of the Classification attribute page in the System Console. 'Attribute Management' is the name of the System Console page it returns to and should match that page's translated title.

admin.global_attributes.classification.m.defaultMessage: Presets and marking colors are configured on Classification Markings.

admin.global_attributes.classification.n.defaultMessage: An attribute named "{name}" already exists but is not part of classification. Rename or remove it in Attribute Management, then reload this page.
