Notice shown to admins when a user attribute named like the classification attribute already exists but is not the classification attribute. {name} is that attribute's display name (not localized). "Attribute Management" is the name of the current System Console section.
Fallback name of the classification attribute. It is inserted into the page heading 'Edit {name} Attribute' in the System Console when the attribute has no display name.

admin.global_attributes.classification.n.defaultMessage: Classification is not set up yet. Enable it on the {link} page first.
admin.global_attributes.classification.n.description: Notice on the Classification attribute page in the System Console when classification markings are not enabled yet. {link} is a link whose text is the localized page name 'Classification Markings'.

admin.global_attributes.classification.o.description: Link button (with an open-in-new icon) after the classification levels note on the Classification attribute page in the System Console. Opens the Classification Markings page. 'Open' is a verb.

admin.global_attributes.classification.r.defaultMessage: This deletes the classification value on every channel that has one. It cannot be undone from Mattermost.
admin.global_attributes.classification.r.description: Body of the confirmation dialog shown when an admin removes Channels from the resources the Classification attribute applies to, in the System Console. Warns that every channel's classification value will be deleted permanently.
Destructive confirm button in the dialog that stops applying Classification to channels, in the System Console. It removes the Channels resource and deletes the stored channel values.
Title of the confirmation dialog shown when an admin removes Channels from the resources the Classification attribute applies to, in the System Console. 'Classification' is the attribute's name.

admin.global_attributes.classification.s.description: Button in the footer of the Classification attribute page in the System Console that saves changes.

admin.global_attributes.classification.s.defaultMessage: Something went wrong while saving. Please try again.
admin.global_attributes.classification.s.description: Error shown next to the Save button on the Classification attribute page in the System Console when saving fails.

admin.global_attributes.classification.s.defaultMessage: Choose the resources this attribute applies to, and how it behaves on each.
admin.global_attributes.classification.s.description: Subtitle under the 'Edit Classification Attribute' heading in the System Console. 'Resources' are the object types an attribute can apply to, such as Users and Channels.

admin.global_attributes.confirm.delete.b.defaultMessage: Deleting this attribute will permanently remove its definition. This action cannot be undone.
admin.global_attributes.confirm.delete.b.description: Body text of the confirmation dialog shown before deleting an attribute definition from System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management.

admin.global_attributes.confirm.delete.e.defaultMessage: An error occurred while deleting this attribute. Please try again.
admin.global_attributes.confirm.delete.e.description: Error banner shown above the attributes table after a delete request fails for an unspecified reason.

admin.global_attributes.confirm.delete.e.defaultMessage: This attribute can't be deleted because other attributes are still linked to it. Remove those links first, then try again.
admin.global_attributes.confirm.delete.e.description: Error banner shown above the attributes table when the server returns 409 on delete because other attributes are linked to this one (i.e. it is used as a template).

admin.global_attributes.confirm.delete.o.defaultMessage: This attribute was created by the plugin "{pluginId}", which is no longer installed.
admin.global_attributes.confirm.delete.o.description: Extra paragraph in the delete-attribute confirmation dialog, shown only when the attribute came from a plugin that is no longer installed. {pluginId} is the raw plugin identifier string (not translated); it falls back to the literal "unknown".

admin.global_attributes.confirm.delete.o.defaultMessage: This attribute was managed by {pluginIds}, which {count, plural, one {is} other {are}} no longer installed.
admin.global_attributes.confirm.delete.o.description: Extra paragraph in the delete-attribute confirmation dialog, shown when every integration that owned the attribute has been uninstalled. {pluginIds} is a localized list of raw plugin identifiers (not translated); {count} is how many there are and selects singular or plural.

admin.global_attributes.confirm.delete.t.description: Title of the delete confirmation dialog in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management. {name} is the attribute's display name. "Delete" is a verb (imperative).

admin.global_attributes.confirm.notify_c.defaultMessage: {count, plural, one {# channel has} other {# channels have}} no channel admin and won't be notified.
admin.global_attributes.confirm.notify_c.description: Bullet in the System Console confirmation modal shown before notifying all channel admins about a missing channel attribute value; {count} is the number of affected channels that have no channel admin, so nobody will be reminded about them.

admin.global_attributes.confirm.notify_c.defaultMessage: Notifications go to each unique channel admin — not one message per channel — so {adminCount, plural, one {# admin} other {# admins}} will be contacted for {channelCount, plural, one {# channel} other {# channels}}.
admin.global_attributes.confirm.notify_c.description: Bullet in the System Console confirmation modal shown before notifying all channel admins about a missing channel attribute value explaining that each channel admin gets one message covering all their channels; {adminCount} is the number of admins and {channelCount} the number of channels.
Confirm button of the System Console confirmation modal shown before notifying all channel admins about a missing channel attribute value.
Label above the preview of the direct message that will be sent, in the System Console confirmation modal shown before notifying all channel admins about a missing channel attribute value.

admin.global_attributes.confirm.notify_c.defaultMessage: {count, plural, one {# channel needs} other {# channels need}} a {attribute} value.
admin.global_attributes.confirm.notify_c.description: Summary line of the System Console confirmation modal shown before notifying all channel admins about a missing channel attribute value; {count} is the number of channels with no value and {attribute} is the attribute's name.
Title of the System Console confirmation modal shown before notifying all channel admins about a missing channel attribute value.

admin.global_attributes.confirm.remove_a.defaultMessage: This will permanently delete every value stored for this attribute on {resources}. This action cannot be undone.
admin.global_attributes.confirm.remove_a.description: Body of the confirmation dialog before removing an attribute from resources, warning that stored values are deleted. {resources} is a list of resource names.
Confirm button of the dialog that removes an attribute from resources and saves the change.

Title of the confirmation dialog shown from the attribute details page in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management before removing an attribute from resources. {resources} is a list of resource names.

admin.global_attributes.filter.resource_.description: Label of the Resource type filter beside the Source filter above the attributes table in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management. The filter narrows the table to attributes that apply to one kind of resource (users, channels or posts).
Option of the Resource type filter in System Console > Attribute Management that shows attributes for every resource type. The default.
Screen-reader label of the open Resource type filter menu in System Console > Attribute Management.
Screen-reader label of the Resource type filter control in System Console > Attribute Management, which opens a menu of resource types (users, channels, posts).

admin.global_attributes.filter.source.description: Label of the Source filter beside the search field above the attributes table in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management. The filter narrows the table to attributes from one source.

admin.global_attributes.filter.source.al.description: Option of the Source filter in System Console > Attribute Management that shows attributes from every source. The default.

admin.global_attributes.filter.source.ld.description: Option of the Source filter in System Console > Attribute Management that shows only attributes synced from LDAP. Product name; usually left untranslated.

admin.global_attributes.filter.source.ma.description: Option of the Source filter in System Console > Attribute Management that shows only attributes defined in Mattermost itself: not synced from an identity provider and not created or owned by a plugin or service.

admin.global_attributes.filter.source.me.description: Screen-reader label of the open Source filter menu in System Console > Attribute Management.
Screen-reader label of the Source filter control in System Console > Attribute Management, which opens a menu of attribute sources.

admin.global_attributes.filter.source.op.description: Option of the Source filter in System Console > Attribute Management that shows only attributes synced from OpenID Connect. Product name; usually left untranslated.

admin.global_attributes.filter.source.pl.description: Option of the Source filter in System Console > Attribute Management that shows only attributes created or owned by a plugin.

admin.global_attributes.filter.source.sa.description: Option of the Source filter in System Console > Attribute Management that shows only attributes synced from SAML. Product name; usually left untranslated.

admin.global_attributes.name_conflict.de.defaultMessage: Another attribute already uses this name.
admin.global_attributes.name_conflict.de.description: Name-conflict notice shown on the attribute details page in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management when another attribute already uses this name. Shown as a danger notice when the match is exact (Users would be blocked) and a warning notice otherwise.

admin.global_attributes.name_conflict.li.defaultMessage: A user attribute named "{name}" already exists and is linked to {owner}. Policies that use user.attributes.{name} read {owner}'s options, not this attribute's.
admin.global_attributes.name_conflict.li.description: Warning in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management when another attribute already owns a user attribute of this name. {name} is that attribute's unique name and {owner} is the display name of the attribute it belongs to. 'user.attributes.' is literal policy syntax and must stay English.

admin.global_attributes.name_conflict.st.defaultMessage: A standalone user attribute named "{name}" already exists. Policies that use user.attributes.{name} read that attribute, not this one.
admin.global_attributes.name_conflict.st.description: Warning in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management when a user attribute of this name exists on its own rather than belonging to another attribute. {name} is its unique name. 'user.attributes.' is literal policy syntax and must stay English.

admin.global_attributes.name_conflict.us.description: Secondary label under the disabled Users option in the 'Add resource' menu on the attribute details page in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management, saying why it cannot be chosen.

admin.global_attributes.new_attribute.description: Label of the primary button at the top of System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management that opens the attribute creation page. "New" is an adjective; keep it identical to the creation page heading.

admin.global_attributes.owners.scoped.description: One entry in the list of integrations that own an attribute, used inside the "Managed by" text in System Console > Attribute Management. {owner} is the integration's display name; {scopes} is a comma-separated list of the scopes it owns (not translated).

admin.global_attributes.search.placehold.description: Placeholder in the search box above the attributes table in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management. 'Search' is a verb.

admin.global_attributes.subtitle.defaultMessage: Define an attribute once, then choose which resources can use it.
admin.global_attributes.subtitle.description: Subtitle line under the "Attribute Management" heading in System Console > System Attributes. "resources" means the object types (Users, Channels, Posts) an attribute can be attached to.

admin.global_attributes.table.actions.cl.description: Tooltip and screen-reader label for the external-link icon on the read-only Classification Markings row of the attributes table; it navigates to the separate Classification Markings admin page. "Open" is a verb.

admin.global_attributes.table.actions.de.description: Menu item in the per-row "More actions" menu of the attributes table. Verb phrase.

admin.global_attributes.table.actions.ed.description: Menu item in the per-row "More actions" menu of the attributes table (currently disabled). Verb phrase.

admin.global_attributes.table.actions.me.description: Accessible name of the per-row actions dropdown menu in the attributes table.

admin.global_attributes.table.actions.ow.description: Secondary label next to the disabled Delete item in the attributes table row menu, explaining that integrations own the attribute so it cannot be deleted here. {owners} is a localized list of the integrations that own the attribute (for example "SCIM and svc-sync").

admin.global_attributes.table.actions.pl.description: Secondary label next to the disabled Delete item in the attributes table row menu, explaining that the attribute is owned by an installed plugin and cannot be removed here.

admin.global_attributes.table.actions.to.description: Tooltip and accessible name for the three-dots button that opens the per-row actions menu in the attributes table.

admin.global_attributes.table.actions.vi.description: Row action in the attributes table in System Console > System Attributes > Attribute Management; opens an attribute that cannot be edited.

admin.global_attributes.table.applies_to.description: Column header in the attributes table listing which resource types (Users, Channels, Posts) the attribute is attached to.

admin.global_attributes.table.attribute.description: Column header in the attributes table for the attribute's display name.

admin.global_attributes.table.attribute..description: Small subtitle shown under the name in the attributes table for the built-in Classification Markings row, indicating it cannot be edited from this screen.

admin.global_attributes.table.clear_filt.description: Button in the attributes table empty state in System Console > Attribute Management that clears the search text and resets every filter to All.

admin.global_attributes.table.empty.defaultMessage: No attributes yet. Click "New attribute" to create one.
admin.global_attributes.table.empty.description: Empty-state message shown in place of the attributes table when no attributes exist. The quoted "New attribute" refers to the button above the table and should match that button's translation.

admin.global_attributes.table.empty_filt.defaultMessage: No attributes match your search or filters.
admin.global_attributes.table.empty_filt.description: Empty-state message in the attributes table in System Console > Attribute Management, shown when the search text and the selected filters together match no attributes.

admin.global_attributes.table.empty_sear.description: Empty-state message in the attributes table in System Console > Attribute Management, shown when the search text matches no attributes.

admin.global_attributes.table.load_error.defaultMessage: There was an error while loading attributes.
admin.global_attributes.table.load_error.description: Error message displayed in place of the attributes table when fetching the attribute list fails.

admin.global_attributes.table.options.description: Column header in the attributes table for the attribute's preset option values. Noun, plural.

admin.global_attributes.table.options.co.description: Cell value in the Options column of the attributes table, giving how many preset option values the attribute defines. # is the count.

admin.global_attributes.table.options.fr.description: Cell value in the Options column of the attributes table for Text-type attributes, which have no preset options because a value is typed in freely.

admin.global_attributes.table.source.description: Column header in the attributes table indicating where the attribute's values come from.

admin.global_attributes.table.source.cla.description: Value in the Source column of the attributes table for the built-in Classification Markings attribute. This is the product feature name.

admin.global_attributes.table.source.man.description: Value in the Source column of the attributes table meaning the attribute's values are maintained inside Mattermost rather than synced from an external directory. "here" refers to this admin console screen.

admin.global_attributes.table.source.own.description: Value in the Source column of the attributes table in System Console > Attribute Management when integrations own the attribute and set its values. {owners} is a localized list of the integrations that own the attribute (for example "SCIM and svc-sync").

admin.global_attributes.table.type.description: Column header in the attributes table for the attribute's data type.

admin.global_attributes.table.type.email.description: Attribute type name shown in the Type column of the attributes table and in the type picker in System Console > Attribute Management. The type holds an email address.

admin.global_attributes.table.type.fallb.description: Value in the Type column of the attributes table for an attribute whose type is not one of the known types. Means "other/unrecognized".

admin.global_attributes.table.type.graph.description: Attribute type name shown in the Type column and type field in System Console > Attribute Management, for attributes whose values form a parent/child hierarchy. The same type is labeled 'Graph' on the User Attributes page.

admin.global_attributes.table.type.multi.description: Value in the Type column of the attributes table: an attribute where several preset options can be chosen at once.

admin.global_attributes.table.type.phone.description: Attribute type name shown in the Type column and type picker in System Console > Attribute Management. The type holds a phone number.

admin.global_attributes.table.type.rank.description: Value in the Type column of the attributes table: an attribute whose options carry an explicit ordering (rank). Adjective describing the attribute.

admin.global_attributes.table.type.selec.description: Value in the Type column of the attributes table: an attribute where exactly one preset option is chosen. Noun/adjective naming the field type, not a verb.

admin.global_attributes.table.type.text.description: Value in the Type column of the attributes table: a free-text attribute. Names the field type.

admin.global_attributes.table.type.url.description: Attribute type name shown in the Type column and type picker in System Console > Attribute Management. The type holds a web address.

admin.global_attributes.title.description: Page header of the Attribute Management (global attributes) section in the System Console.

admin.google.authTitle.description: Setting label for a text field in the Google OAuth admin settings; the OAuth authorization endpoint URL. Ends with a colon.

admin.google.clientIdDescription.defaultMessage: The Client ID you received when registering your application with Google.

admin.google.clientSecretExample.description: Placeholder text inside the Google Client Secret field showing an example secret value.

admin.google.clientSecretTitle.description: Setting label for a text field in the Google OAuth admin settings; ends with a colon.

admin.google.discoveryEndpointDesc.defaultMessage: The URL of the discovery document for OpenID Connect with Google.

admin.google.EnableMarkdownDesc.defaultMessage: 1. Log in to your Google account. 2. Go to https://console.developers.google.com, click Credentials in the left hand side. 3. Under the Credentials header, click Create credentials, choose OAuth client ID and select Web Application. 4. Enter "Mattermost - your-company-name" as the Name. 5. Under Authorized redirect URIs enter "your-mattermost-url/signup/google/complete" (example: http://localhost:8065/signup/google/complete). Click Create. 6. Paste the Client ID and Client Secret to the fields below, then click Save. 7. Go to the Google People API and click Enable.

admin.google.tokenTitle.description: Setting label for a text field in the Google OAuth admin settings; the OAuth token endpoint URL. Ends with a colon.

admin.google.userTitle.description: Setting label for a text field in the Google OAuth admin settings; the API endpoint used to fetch the user profile. Ends with a colon.

admin.group_settings.group_detail.groupU.defaultMessage: Listing of users in Mattermost associated with this group.

admin.ldap.adminFilterFilterDescHover.defaultMessage:
The users selected by the query will have access to your Mattermost server as System Admins. By default, System Admins have complete access to the Mattermost System Console. Existing members that are identified by this attribute will be promoted from member to System Admin upon next login. The next login is based upon Session lengths set in System Console > Session Lengths. It is highly recommended to manually demote users to members in System Console > User Management to ensure access is restricted immediately.
 
Note: If this filter is removed/changed, System Admins that were promoted via this filter will be demoted to members and will not retain access to the System Console. When this filter is not in use, System Admins can be manually promoted/demoted in System Console > User Management.

admin.ldap.syncIntervalHelpText.defaultMessage: AD/LDAP Synchronization updates Mattermost user information to reflect updates on the AD/LDAP server. For example, when a user's name changes on the AD/LDAP server, the change updates in Mattermost when synchronization is performed. Mattermost performs synchronization on the interval entered. For example, if 60 is entered, Mattermost synchronizes every 60 minutes.

admin.saml.adminAttrDesc.defaultMessage:
(Optional) The attribute in the SAML Assertion for designating System Admins. The users selected by the query will have access to your Mattermost server as System Admins. By default, System Admins have complete access to the Mattermost System Console.
 
Existing members that are identified by this attribute will be promoted from member to System Admin upon next login. The next login is based upon Session lengths set in **System Console > Session Lengths**. It is highly recommended to manually demote users to members in **System Console > User Management** to ensure access is restricted immediately.
 
Note: If this filter is removed/changed, System Admins that were promoted via this filter will be demoted to members and will not retain access to the System Console. When this filter is not in use, System Admins can be manually promoted/demoted in **System Console > User Management**.

admin.service.disableBotOwnerDeactivated.defaultMessage: Disable bot accounts when owner is deactivated:
admin.service.disableBotOwnerDeactivated.description: Admin console label for a true/false setting that disables a user's bot accounts when that user is deactivated; ends with a colon before the radio buttons.

admin.service.disableBotWhenOwnerIsDeact.defaultMessage: When a user is deactivated, disables all bot accounts managed by the user. To re-enable bot accounts, go to [Integrations > Bot Accounts]({siteURL}/_redirect/integrations/bots).
admin.service.disableBotWhenOwnerIsDeact.description: Admin console help text for the disable-bots-on-owner-deactivation setting; supports Markdown; {siteURL} is the server's base URL inside a link to the Bot Accounts page.

admin.service.enableBotAccountCreation.defaultMessage: When true, System Admins can create bot accounts for integrations in <linkBots>Integrations > Bot Accounts</linkBots>. Bot accounts are similar to user accounts except they cannot be used to log in. See <linkDocumentation>documentation</linkDocumentation> to learn more.
admin.service.enableBotAccountCreation.description: Admin console help text for the 'Enable Bot Account Creation' toggle; <linkBots> wraps a link to the Bot Accounts page and <linkDocumentation> wraps 'documentation' as a hyperlink.

admin.service.enableBotTitle.description: Admin console label for a true/false setting allowing creation of bot accounts; ends with a colon and trailing space before the radio buttons.

admin.service.enableChannelViewedMessage.description: Label of the toggle in System Console > Environment > Web Server that controls whether channel_viewed WebSocket events are emitted. Keep the trailing colon.

admin.service.enableChannelViewedMessage.defaultMessage: This setting determines whether `channel_viewed` WebSocket events are sent, which synchronize unread notifications across clients and devices. Disabling the setting in larger deployments may improve server performance.
admin.service.enableChannelViewedMessage.description: Help text under the "Enable Channel Viewed WebSocket Messages" toggle in System Console > Environment > Web Server. `channel_viewed` is a literal event name in backticks and must not be translated (it renders as plain text, not Markdown).

admin.service.enforceMfaDesc.defaultMessage:
When true, <link>multi-factor authentication</link> is required for login. New users will be required to configure MFA on signup. Logged in users without MFA configured are redirected to the MFA setup page until configuration is complete.
 
If your system has users with login methods other than AD/LDAP and email, MFA must be enforced with the authentication provider outside of Mattermost.
admin.service.enforceMfaDesc.description: Admin console help text for the 'Enforce Multi-factor Authentication' toggle; <link> wraps 'multi-factor authentication' as a documentation hyperlink.

admin.service.enforceMfaTitle.description: Admin console label for a true/false setting making MFA mandatory at login; ends with a colon before the radio buttons.

admin.service.extendSessionLengthActivit.defaultMessage: When true, sessions will be automatically extended when the user is active in their Mattermost client. User sessions will only expire if they are not active in their Mattermost client for the entire duration of the session lengths defined in the fields below. When false, sessions will not extend with activity in Mattermost. User sessions will immediately expire at the end of the session length or idle timeouts defined below.
admin.service.extendSessionLengthActivit.description: Admin console help text for the 'Extend session length with activity' toggle on the Session Lengths page; trailing space is intentional.
Label of a true/false setting in the System Console > Session Lengths page; trailing space separates it from the radio buttons that follow.

admin.service.forward80To443.description: Admin console label for a true/false web server setting that redirects insecure HTTP (port 80) traffic to HTTPS (port 443); ends with a colon before the radio buttons.

admin.service.forward80To443Description.defaultMessage: Forwards all insecure traffic from port 80 to secure port 443. Not recommended when using a proxy server.
admin.service.forward80To443Description.description: Help text for the Forward port 80 to 443 setting on the System Console Web Server page.

admin.service.forward80To443Description..defaultMessage:
Forwards all insecure traffic from port 80 to secure port 443. Not recommended when using a proxy server.
 
This setting cannot be enabled until your server is [listening](#ServiceSettings.ListenAddress) on port 443.
admin.service.forward80To443Description..description: Help text variant for the Forward port 80 to 443 setting shown when it cannot be enabled; contains a markdown link [listening](#...) to another setting — keep the link target unchanged.

admin.service.googleDescription.defaultMessage: Set this key to enable the display of titles for embedded YouTube video previews. Without the key, YouTube previews will still be created based on hyperlinks appearing in messages or comments but they will not show the video title. View a <link>Google Developers Tutorial</link> for instructions on how to obtain a key and add YouTube Data API v3 as a service to your key.
admin.service.googleDescription.description: Admin console help text for the Google API Key setting used for YouTube preview titles; <link> wraps 'Google Developers Tutorial' as a hyperlink.

admin.service.googleExample.description: Placeholder text showing an example API key string for the Google API Key input; the key is a random literal example.

admin.service.googleTitle.description: Admin console label for the text input holding a Google API key (used for YouTube video previews); ends with a colon.

admin.service.hardenedModeDesc.defaultMessage: Enables a hardened mode for Mattermost that makes user experience trade-offs in the interest of security. See <link>documentation</link> to learn more.
admin.service.hardenedModeDesc.description: Admin console help text under the Enable Hardened Mode toggle on the System Console > Environment > Web Server page; <link> wraps the word documentation and points to Mattermost docs. Markdown is disabled for this string, so ** has no effect. Moved here from the Experimental Features page.

admin.service.hardenedModeTitle.description: Setting label (toggle) on the System Console > Environment > Web Server page for a security-focused mode; ends with a colon. Moved here from the Experimental Features page.

admin.service.iconDescription.defaultMessage: When true, webhooks, slash commands and other integrations will be allowed to change the profile picture they post with. Note: Combined with allowing integrations to override usernames, users may be able to perform phishing attacks by attempting to impersonate other users.
admin.service.iconDescription.description: Admin console help text for the toggle allowing integrations to override the profile picture they post with; warns about phishing risk.

admin.service.iconTitle.defaultMessage: Enable integrations to override profile picture icons:
admin.service.iconTitle.description: Admin console label for a true/false integrations setting; ends with a colon before the radio buttons.

admin.service.insecureTlsDesc.defaultMessage: When true, any outgoing HTTPS requests will accept unverified, self-signed certificates. For example, outgoing webhooks to a server with a self-signed TLS certificate, using any domain, will be allowed. Note that this makes these connections susceptible to man-in-the-middle attacks.
admin.service.insecureTlsDesc.description: Admin console help text for the 'Enable Insecure Outgoing Connections' toggle; warns about man-in-the-middle attack risk.

admin.service.insecureTlsProductionWarni.defaultMessage: Mattermost will not verify TLS certificates for outbound connections, exposing them to man-in-the-middle attacks. Enable only for testing.
admin.service.insecureTlsProductionWarni.description: Body of the red danger notice under the "Enable Insecure Outgoing Connections" toggle in System Console > Environment > Web Server, shown once the admin turns it on.

admin.service.insecureTlsProductionWarni.defaultMessage: Insecure outgoing connections are not recommended for production environments
admin.service.insecureTlsProductionWarni.description: Title of the red danger notice under the "Enable Insecure Outgoing Connections" toggle in System Console > Environment > Web Server.

admin.service.insecureTlsTitle.description: Admin console label for a true/false setting allowing outgoing HTTPS connections with unverified certificates; ends with a colon and trailing space before the radio buttons.

admin.service.integrationRequestDesc.defaultMessage: The number of seconds to wait for Integration requests. That includes <slashCommands>Slash Commands</slashCommands>, <outgoingWebhooks>Outgoing Webhooks</outgoingWebhooks>, <interactiveMessages>Interactive Messages</interactiveMessages> and <interactiveDialogs>Interactive Dialogs</interactiveDialogs>.
admin.service.integrationRequestDesc.description: Admin console help text for the integration request timeout setting; the four tag pairs (<slashCommands>, <outgoingWebhooks>, <interactiveMessages>, <interactiveDialogs>) each wrap a documentation hyperlink.

admin.service.integrationRequestTitle.description: Admin console label for a numeric setting (seconds) for integration request timeouts; ends with a colon and trailing space.

admin.service.internalConnectionsDesc.defaultMessage: A whitelist of local network addresses that can be requested by the Mattermost server on behalf of a client. Care should be used when configuring this setting to prevent unintended access to your local network. See <link>documentation</link> to learn more. Changing this requires a server restart before taking effect.
admin.service.internalConnectionsDesc.description: Admin console help text for the untrusted internal connections whitelist setting; <link> wraps 'documentation' as a hyperlink.

admin.service.internalConnectionsEx.description: Placeholder text showing example values (a hostname, an IP, and a CIDR range, space-separated) for the internal connections whitelist input; literal examples.

admin.service.internalConnectionsTitle.description: Admin console label for a text setting listing local addresses the server may request on behalf of clients; ends with a colon and trailing space; the value completes the sentence.

admin.service.letsEncryptCertificateCach.description: Admin console label for the text input holding the file path where Let's Encrypt certificates are cached; "Let's Encrypt" is a certificate authority brand name; ends with a colon.

admin.service.letsEncryptCertificateCach.defaultMessage: Certificates retrieved and other data about the Let's Encrypt service will be stored in this file.
admin.service.letsEncryptCertificateCach.description: Help text for the Let's Encrypt certificate cache file setting on the System Console Web Server page.

admin.service.listenAddress.description: Admin console label for the web server bind address text input; ends with a colon.

admin.service.listenDescription.defaultMessage: The address and port to which to bind and listen. Specifying ":8065" will bind to all network interfaces. Specifying "127.0.0.1:8065" will only bind to the network interface having that IP address. If you choose a port of a lower level (called "system ports" or "well-known ports", in the range of 0-1023), you must have permissions to bind to that port. On Linux you can use: "sudo setcap cap_net_bind_service=+ep ./bin/mattermost" to allow Mattermost to bind to well-known ports.
admin.service.listenDescription.description: Admin console help text for the Listen Address setting; quoted values like ":8065" and the sudo command are literal and should not be translated.

admin.service.listenExample.description: Placeholder text showing an example bind address (port only) for the Listen Address input.

admin.service.managedResourcePaths.description: Admin console label for a text setting listing URL paths managed by the desktop app (opened within the app rather than a browser); ends with a colon.

admin.service.managedResourcePathsDescri.defaultMessage: A comma-separated list of paths on the Mattermost server that are managed by another service. See <link>here</link> for more information.
admin.service.managedResourcePathsDescri.description: Help text for the Managed Resource Paths setting on the System Console Web Server page; <link> wraps a documentation link.

admin.service.maximumPayloadSize.description: Admin console label for a numeric web server setting capping API request payload size in bytes; ends with a colon.

admin.service.maximumPayloadSizeDescript.defaultMessage: The maximum number of bytes allowed in the payload of incoming HTTP calls
admin.service.maximumPayloadSizeDescript.description: Help text for the Maximum Payload Size setting on the System Console Web Server page.

admin.service.mfaDesc.defaultMessage: When true, users with AD/LDAP or email login can add multi-factor authentication to their account using an authenticator app.
admin.service.mfaDesc.description: Admin console help text for the 'Enable Multi-factor Authentication' toggle.

admin.service.mfaTitle.description: Admin console label for a true/false setting letting users add MFA to their accounts; ends with a colon before the radio buttons.

admin.service.minimumHashtagLengthDescri.defaultMessage: Minimum number of characters in a hashtag. This must be greater than or equal to 2.
admin.service.minimumHashtagLengthDescri.description: Admin console help text for the Minimum Hashtag Length number setting on the Database page.

admin.service.minimumHashtagLengthExampl.description: Placeholder in the Minimum Hashtag Length input showing an example value.

admin.service.minimumHashtagLengthTitle.description: Admin console number setting name for the minimum characters required in a hashtag; ends with a colon.

admin.service.mobileSessionHours.description: Label of a numeric input in the System Console > Session Lengths page; sets how many hours a mobile app session lasts.

admin.service.mobileSessionHoursDesc.defaultMessage: The number of hours from the last time a user entered their credentials to the expiry of the user's session. After changing this setting, the new session length will take effect after the next time the user enters their credentials.
admin.service.mobileSessionHoursDesc.description: Help text for the mobile session length setting on the System Console Session Lengths page.

admin.service.mobileSessionHoursDesc.ext.defaultMessage: Set the number of hours from the last activity in Mattermost to the expiry of the user's session on mobile. After changing this setting, the new session length will take effect after the next time the user enters their credentials.
admin.service.mobileSessionHoursDesc.ext.description: Help text variant for the mobile session length setting, shown when 'extend session length with activity' is enabled.

admin.service.outgoingOAuthConnectionsDe.defaultMessage: When true, outgoing webhooks and slash commands will use the configured OAuth connections to authenticate with third party services. See <link>documentation</link> to learn more.
admin.service.outgoingOAuthConnectionsDe.description: Admin console help text for the 'Enable Outgoing OAuth Connections' toggle; <link> wraps 'documentation' as a hyperlink.

admin.service.outgoingOAuthConnectionsTi.description: Admin console label for a true/false setting letting webhooks and slash commands authenticate with third parties via OAuth; ends with a colon and trailing space before the radio buttons.

admin.service.outWebhooksDesc.defaultMessage: When true, outgoing webhooks will be allowed. See <link>documentation</link> to learn more.
admin.service.outWebhooksDesc.description: Admin console help text for the 'Enable Outgoing Webhooks' toggle; <link> wraps 'documentation' as a hyperlink.

admin.service.outWebhooksTitle.description: Admin console label for a true/false setting allowing outgoing webhook integrations; ends with a colon and trailing space before the radio buttons.

admin.service.overrideDescription.defaultMessage: When true, webhooks, slash commands and other integrations will be allowed to change the username they are posting as. Note: Combined with allowing integrations to override profile picture icons, users may be able to perform phishing attacks by attempting to impersonate other users.
admin.service.overrideDescription.description: Admin console help text for the toggle allowing integrations to override the username they post as; warns about phishing risk.

admin.service.overrideTitle.description: Admin console label for a true/false integrations setting; ends with a colon before the radio buttons.

admin.service.performanceDebuggingDescri.defaultMessage: When true, users can access debugging settings for their account in **Settings > Advanced > Performance Debugging** to assist in diagnosing performance issues. Changing this requires a server restart before taking effect.
admin.service.performanceDebuggingDescri.description: Admin console help text for the 'Enable Client Performance Debugging' toggle; supports Markdown ('**Settings > Advanced > Performance Debugging**' renders bold).

admin.service.performanceDebuggingTitle.description: Admin console label for a true/false setting exposing performance-debugging options to end users; ends with a colon and trailing space before the radio buttons.

admin.service.personalAccessTokenMaxLife.defaultMessage: The maximum number of days a personal access token can remain valid before it expires. Set to 0 to allow tokens that never expire. When set to a positive value, users must select an expiry date within this range when creating a token.
admin.service.personalAccessTokenMaxLife.description: Admin console help text for the maximum personal access token lifetime setting; 0 is a literal value meaning no expiry.
Admin console label for a numeric setting (days) capping personal access token validity; ends with a colon.

admin.service.readTimeout.description: Admin console label for a numeric web server setting: how long the server waits when reading an incoming request; ends with a colon.

admin.service.readTimeoutDescription.defaultMessage: Maximum time allowed from when the connection is accepted to when the request body is fully read.
admin.service.readTimeoutDescription.description: Help text for the Read Timeout setting on the System Console Web Server page; describes an HTTP request read timeout.

admin.service.revokeNonCompliantTokens.b.description: Button label in the System Console session settings that revokes personal access tokens exceeding the configured maximum lifetime.

admin.service.revokeNonCompliantTokens.c.defaultMessage: This will permanently revoke {count, number} personal access {count, plural, one {token} other {tokens}} that {count, plural, one {does} other {do}} not comply with the current maximum lifetime policy, including tokens for user-owned bot accounts. Plugin-owned bot account tokens are exempt. This cannot be undone.
admin.service.revokeNonCompliantTokens.c.description: Body text of the confirmation dialog before revoking non-compliant personal access tokens; {count} is the number of tokens, with plural branches adjusting 'token(s)' and the verb 'does/do'.
Confirm button label in the dialog that revokes non-compliant personal access tokens.
Title of the confirmation dialog asking the admin whether to revoke non-compliant personal access tokens.

admin.service.revokeNonCompliantTokens.c.defaultMessage: {count, number} personal access {count, plural, one {token} other {tokens}} currently {count, plural, one {violates} other {violate}} the maximum lifetime policy.
admin.service.revokeNonCompliantTokens.c.description: Status text under the revoke button showing how many tokens violate the maximum lifetime policy; {count} is the number, with plural branches for 'token(s)' and 'violates/violate'.

admin.service.revokeNonCompliantTokens.e.description: Error message shown when revoking non-compliant tokens fails; {error} is the server error message.

admin.service.revokeNonCompliantTokens.n.defaultMessage: No personal access tokens currently need to be revoked.
admin.service.revokeNonCompliantTokens.n.description: Status text under the revoke button when there are no personal access tokens violating the lifetime policy.

admin.service.revokeNonCompliantTokens.s.defaultMessage: Revoked {count, number} non-compliant personal access {count, plural, one {token} other {tokens}}.
admin.service.revokeNonCompliantTokens.s.description: Success message after revoking non-compliant tokens; {count} is the number revoked, with a plural branch for 'token(s)'.

admin.service.revokeNonCompliantTokensDe.defaultMessage: Permanently revokes all existing personal access tokens that do not comply with the maximum lifetime above (tokens that never expire or expire beyond the cap), including tokens for user-owned bot accounts. Plugin-owned bot account tokens are exempt. The maximum lifetime only applies to newly created tokens, so use this to bring already-issued tokens into compliance. You will be shown how many tokens are affected before confirming.
admin.service.revokeNonCompliantTokensDe.description: Admin console help text below the 'Revoke non-compliant tokens' button, explaining which personal access tokens will be permanently revoked.

admin.service.revokeNonCompliantTokensTi.description: Button label (with colon) in the admin console; permanently revokes personal access tokens exceeding the configured maximum lifetime; 'Revoke' is a verb.

admin.service.sessionCache.description: Label of a numeric input in the System Console > Session Lengths page; sets how many minutes a session is cached in memory.

admin.service.sessionCacheDesc.defaultMessage: The number of minutes to cache a session in memory:
admin.service.sessionCacheDesc.description: Help text (with trailing colon) for the Session Cache setting on the System Console Session Lengths page.

admin.service.sessionHoursEx.description: Placeholder showing an example value inside the hour-based session length inputs in the System Console; keep the quotes and the number as an example.

admin.service.sessionIdleTimeout.description: Label of a numeric input in the System Console > Session Lengths page; sets the idle minutes before a session expires.

admin.service.sessionIdleTimeoutDesc.defaultMessage:
The number of minutes from the last time a user was active on the system to the expiry of the user's session. Once expired, the user will need to log in to continue. Minimum is 5 minutes, and 0 is unlimited.
 
Applies to the desktop app and browsers. For mobile apps, use an EMM provider to lock the app when not in use. In High Availability mode, enable IP hash load balancing for reliable timeout measurement.
admin.service.sessionIdleTimeoutDesc.description: Help text for the Session Idle Timeout setting on the System Console Session Lengths page; multi-paragraph.

admin.service.sessionIdleTimeoutEx.description: Placeholder example value for the Session Idle Timeout input in the System Console.

admin.service.sessionMinutesEx.description: Placeholder showing an example value inside the Session Cache minutes input in the System Console; keep the quotes and the number as an example.

admin.service.siteURL.description: Admin console label for the text input holding the server's base URL; ends with a colon.

admin.service.siteURLDescription.defaultMessage:
The URL that users will use to access Mattermost. Standard ports, such as 80 and 443, can be omitted, but non-standard ports are required. For example: http://example.com:8065. This setting is required.
 
Mattermost may be hosted at a subpath. For example: http://example.com:8065/company/mattermost. A restart is required before the server will work correctly.
admin.service.siteURLDescription.description: Help text for the Site URL setting on the System Console Web Server page; multi-paragraph, URLs are examples.

admin.service.siteURLExample.description: Placeholder example value for the Site URL input on the System Console Web Server page.

admin.service.ssoSessionHours.description: Label of a numeric input in the System Console > Session Lengths page; SSO refers to single sign-on authentication (SAML, GitLab, OAuth).

admin.service.ssoSessionHoursDesc.defaultMessage: The number of hours from the last time a user entered their credentials to the expiry of the user's session. If the authentication method is SAML or GitLab, the user may automatically be logged back in to Mattermost if they are already logged in to SAML or GitLab. After changing this setting, the setting will take effect after the next time the user enters their credentials.
admin.service.ssoSessionHoursDesc.description: Help text for the SSO session length setting on the System Console Session Lengths page; SAML and GitLab are authentication providers.

admin.service.ssoSessionHoursDesc.extend.defaultMessage: Set the number of hours from the last activity in Mattermost to the expiry of the user's session for SSO authentication, such as SAML, GitLab and OAuth 2.0. If the authentication method is SAML or GitLab, the user may automatically be logged back in to Mattermost if they are already logged in to SAML or GitLab. After changing this setting, the setting will take effect after the next time the user enters their credentials.
admin.service.ssoSessionHoursDesc.extend.description: Help text variant for the SSO session length setting, shown when 'extend session length with activity' is enabled.

admin.service.terminateSessionsOnPasswor.defaultMessage: When true, all sessions of a user will expire if their password is changed by themselves or an administrator. If password change is initiated by user, their current session is not terminated.
admin.service.terminateSessionsOnPasswor.description: Help text under the 'Terminate Sessions on Password Change' setting in the System Console > Session Lengths page, for system admins.
Label of a true/false setting in the System Console > Session Lengths page; trailing space separates it from the radio buttons that follow.

admin.service.testingDescription.defaultMessage: When true, the /test slash command is enabled to load test accounts, data, and text formatting. Use this setting only in isolated non-production environments and never in production. Changing this requires a server restart before taking effect.
admin.service.testingDescription.description: Admin console help text for the 'Enable Testing Commands' toggle; '/test' is a literal slash command name.

admin.service.testingProductionWarning.t.description: Body of the red danger notice under the "Enable Testing Commands" toggle in System Console > Environment > Developer. "/test" is a slash command name and stays untranslated.

admin.service.testingProductionWarning.t.defaultMessage: Testing commands are not recommended for production environments
admin.service.testingProductionWarning.t.description: Title of the red danger notice under the "Enable Testing Commands" toggle in System Console > Environment > Developer.

admin.service.testingTitle.description: Admin console label for a true/false setting enabling the /test slash command; ends with a colon before the radio buttons.

admin.service.testSiteURLFail.description: Result message shown after the Test Live URL button on the Site URL setting fails; {error} is the error detail.

admin.service.testSiteURLSuccess.description: Result message shown after the Test Live URL button on the Site URL setting succeeds.

admin.service.testSiteURLTesting.description: Status text shown on/near the Test Live URL button while the site URL test is running; ellipsis indicates progress.

admin.service.tlsCertFile.description: Admin console label for the text input holding the file path to the TLS certificate; ends with a colon.

admin.service.tlsCertFileDescription.description: Help text for the TLS Certificate File setting on the System Console Web Server page.

admin.service.tlsKeyFileDescription.defaultMessage: The private key file to use.
admin.service.tlsKeyFileDescription.description: Help text for the TLS Key File setting on the System Console Web Server page; 'private key' is a cryptographic key file.

admin.service.useLetsEncryptDescription.defaultMessage: Enable the automatic retrieval of certificates from Let's Encrypt. The certificate will be retrieved when a client attempts to connect from a new domain. This will work with multiple domains.
admin.service.useLetsEncryptDescription.description: Help text for the Use Let's Encrypt setting on the System Console Web Server page; Let's Encrypt is a certificate authority (keep name).

admin.service.useLetsEncryptDescription..defaultMessage:
Enable the automatic retrieval of certificates from Let's Encrypt. The certificate will be retrieved when a client attempts to connect from a new domain. This will work with multiple domains.
 
This setting cannot be enabled unless the [Forward port 80 to 443](#ServiceSettings.Forward80To443) setting is set to true.
admin.service.useLetsEncryptDescription..description: Help text variant for the Use Let's Encrypt setting shown when it cannot be enabled; contains a markdown link [Forward port 80 to 443](#...) — keep the link target unchanged.

admin.service.userAccessTokensDescriptio.defaultMessage: When true, users can create personal access tokens for integrations in Profile > Security. They can be used to authenticate against the API and give full access to the account.
